text:
Penobscot County places fifth among Maine counties for 202/PRAC assisted units in 2025
R. N. Clark
Penobscot County placed fifth among nine Maine counties in the 202/PRAC assisted-unit ranking for 2025, with 35 assisted units.
The county's assisted-unit total was unchanged from 2024, remaining at 35.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally reduce rent for low-income households that meet program eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households describes three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households that receive HUD rental assistance typically pay rent equal to 30% of their income after deductions, with the federal government covering the remainder. Eligibility is based on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are generally placed on waiting lists until assistance is available.
| State rank | County | Assisted units |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | York County | 244 |
| 2 | Cumberland County | 154 |
| 3 | Kennebec County | 146 |
| 4 | Lincoln County | 39 |
| 5 | Penobscot County | 35 |
| 6 | Waldo County | 32 |
| 7 | Knox County | 31 |
| 8 | Sagadahoc County | 27 |
| 9 | Hancock County | 26 |
Information in this article was obtained from the assisted housing database maintained by the government-run Office of Policy Development and Research (PD&R). The source data can be found here.
